lesenParts.text:
Moving to a new city is often described as an exciting adventure, but for me, it felt more like a challenge I wasn't ready for. Last summer, my parents announced that we were moving from our quiet village to the bustling city of Manchester. I had lived in the same house for fourteen years, and the thought of leaving my friends and my favourite local park was devastating.

When we first arrived, the noise was the biggest shock. Unlike the peaceful nights I was used to, the city never seemed to sleep. There were sirens, traffic, and people talking at all hours. For the first two weeks, I barely left my room. I felt like an outsider looking in, convinced that I would never fit into this fast-paced environment. I spent most of my time messaging my old friends, feeling sorry for myself.

However, everything changed when I joined a local photography club. I had always enjoyed taking pictures, and I thought it might be a good way to get out of the house. On my first day, I met a girl named Sarah who was also new to the area. We started exploring the city together, looking for interesting buildings and street art to photograph. Through her eyes, I began to see the city differently. Instead of just seeing traffic and noise, I started to notice the beautiful architecture and the vibrant culture.

It has been six months now, and I can honestly say I don't regret the move. While I still miss my old friends, I have built a new life here. I have learned that moving isn't just about changing your address; it is about changing your perspective. You have to be willing to step outside your comfort zone to find the hidden gems in any new place. If you are facing a big move, my advice is to find a hobby or a group that shares your interests. It makes the world feel a lot smaller and much friendlier.

d) Confused by the parents' decision.

lesenParts.textTitle: A Weekend at the Local Food Market
lesenParts.text: Last Saturday, I decided to visit the new food market in the town square. I had heard many people talking about the fresh produce and the friendly atmosphere. (1) __________ I arrived just as the stalls were opening, so it was still quite quiet. The smell of freshly baked bread and roasted coffee beans was everywhere. I walked slowly past the different stalls, looking at the colorful vegetables and local cheeses. (2) __________ I eventually stopped at a small stall that sold homemade honey. The owner was very kind and let me taste three different types before I made my choice. After buying a jar of honey, I felt hungry and looked for something to eat. (3) __________ It was filled with fresh herbs and local vegetables. It was probably the best lunch I have had in a long time. While I was eating, a local band started playing some relaxing music near the fountain. (4) __________ Many families were sitting on the grass, enjoying the sunshine and the music. It was a perfect way to spend a Saturday morning. I will definitely return next weekend to try some of the other delicious treats. (5) __________ It is a great addition to our town and I hope it stays for a long time.

Hello everyone! I am delighted to announce that the Riverside Sports Centre will finally open its doors to the public next Monday. We have spent months preparing the facilities. If you are interested in swimming, our main pool is 25 metres long and has a special area for children. For those who prefer fitness, the gym is equipped with the latest machines, and we offer a variety of classes including yoga and aerobics. We are currently looking for a receptionist to join our team, so please check our website if you are interested. Membership fees are very reasonable, and if you sign up before the end of the month, you will receive a discount of 15 percent on your first year. We also have a cafe on the ground floor where you can relax after your workout. We look forward to seeing you there!

Hello everyone. I am here to give you the final details about our upcoming school trip to France. We will be departing from the school gates at 7:30 am on Monday morning, so please make sure you arrive on time. We are staying at a lovely hotel in the countryside, which is famous for its large swimming pool. On the first day, we will visit a local museum to learn about history. The most exciting part of the trip will be the visit to the chocolate factory on Wednesday, where we can taste everything! For lunch, we will have a picnic in the park, but please remember to bring a bottle of water. Finally, don't forget to bring your camera to take photos of the beautiful scenery. I am sure we will have a fantastic time!

horenParts.transcript: Interviewer: Sarah, you've been blogging for five years now. What made you start? Sarah: I was working in an office and felt bored. I took a trip to Peru and realized I wanted to share my experiences. Interviewer: Was it hard to get started? Sarah: Yes, I didn't know anything about photography or writing for an audience. I had to learn everything from scratch. Interviewer: Many people think travel blogging is just a holiday. What do you say to them? Sarah: It's definitely not! I spend hours editing photos and researching locations. It's a full-time job. Interviewer: Do you ever get lonely? Sarah: Sometimes, but I meet so many interesting people on the road that it balances out. Interviewer: What is your favorite part of the job? Sarah: Seeing a place I've only read about in books. It's magical. Interviewer: Any advice for beginners? Sarah: Be yourself. Don't try to copy other bloggers. Authenticity is what people want to see.
